messages.content: 獲取人類HbA1c、正常血紅蛋白和大鼠血紅蛋白的蛋白質序列和它們的3D模型。

function.name: protein_info_get_sequence_and_3D
function.description: Retrive the sequence and 3D models of proteins. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

model_3d.description: Set true to get 3D model of the protein.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to retrieve the sequences and 3D models of human HbA1c, normal hemoglobin (presumably human HbA), and rat hemoglobin. We need to use the function `protein_info_get_sequence_and_3D`. Provide the arguments accordingly.

We should call the function three times? Or we can combine into one? The function signature expects a single object with protein_name and optional model_3d. It returns "any". So we might need to call it separately for each protein. But maybe we can pass multiple names? The function signature only accepts a single protein_name. So we need to call it thrice.

Thus we will produce calls:

First call: protein_name: "Human HbA1c" or "Hemoglobin A1c"? Actually the protein name could be "Hemoglobin A1c" or "HbA1c". We'll try "Hemoglobin A1c".

Second call: "Human Hemoglobin" or "Hemoglobin A". We'll use "Hemoglobin A".

Third call: "Rat Hemoglobin" or "Hemoglobin Rattus norvegicus". We'll use "Hemoglobin Rattus norvegicus".

We also set model_3d: true (default). So we don't need to specify.

We'll output the calls.
